items.title: Portal Diabetes Gets FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for Implantable Insulin Pump
items.summary: Portal Diabetes (Westfield, Indiana) received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for the Portal Pump — an implantable insulin pump that delivers insulin directly to the abdomen, integrated with CGM technology and a proprietary temperature-stable concentrated insulin. The first two patients have already received Portal Insulin injections in a Phase 1 study in San Diego. The goal: no more meal announcements, exercise announcements, or night wakings — a fully closed loop. Clinical trials for the full combination system are planned around Q4 2027. The Breakthrough designation also qualifies Portal for the TCET pathway, expediting Medicare coverage.
items.relevance: This is the 'functional cure' approach — implantable pump + stable insulin + CGM closing the loop completely. No meal bolusing, no exercise adjustments, no alarms waking you up. If it works as described, it changes everything for T1D families. Q4 2027 clinical trials means real-world data is still 2+ years out, but the FDA Breakthrough designation means they're on the fast track. This is the kind of future tech that AVA's educational mission is building toward — kids learning T1D management today will graduate to systems like this.

items.title: Figma Partners with Anthropic — 'Code to Canvas' Bridges Claude Code and Design
items.summary: Figma announced 'Code to Canvas,' a new feature built in partnership with Anthropic that converts code generated by AI tools like Claude Code into fully editable Figma designs. The workflow: prompt Claude Code to build a UI, then bring the working interface directly into Figma's canvas where teams can refine it, compare options side by side, and align on design decisions. Figma is betting that AI coding tools haven't eliminated the need for design — they've made it more essential. Meanwhile, Figma stock is down 85% from its 52-week high, caught in the broader SaaS sell-off that traders are calling the 'SaaSpocalypse.'
items.relevance: Direct integration between Claude Code and Figma is a big deal for your workflow. You could prototype AVA UI in Claude Code, then push it to Figma for visual refinement — or hand it to a designer who works in Figma. The 'SaaSpocalypse' note is interesting context: AI coding tools are disrupting traditional SaaS so hard that the whole sector is in freefall. Figma is adapting by embracing Claude Code rather than fighting it.

items.title: Xcode 26.3 Brings Agentic Coding — Claude Agent and OpenAI Codex Built Into Xcode
items.summary: Apple released Xcode 26.3 with native support for agentic coding. Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex can now operate directly inside Xcode with access to the full development lifecycle: searching documentation, exploring file structures, updating project settings, capturing Xcode Previews, and iterating through builds and fixes autonomously. The integration uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP) open standard, meaning any compatible agent can plug in. This expands on Xcode 26's coding assistant with a shift from suggestions to autonomous task execution.
items.relevance: Massive for your SwiftUI development on AVA Type 1. Claude Agent running natively in Xcode with access to Previews, build cycles, and project settings means you could have an AI agent iterate on your app's UI in real-time — building, previewing, fixing, and refining without you manually switching contexts. The MCP integration also means Clawdbot could potentially connect to Xcode in the future. This is the tool convergence you've been building toward.

items.title: China's Lunar New Year AI Blitz — Alibaba Qwen3.5, ByteDance Doubao 2.0, Zhipu GLM-5
items.summary: Chinese AI labs dropped a wave of new models ahead of Lunar New Year. Alibaba's Qwen3.5 handles text/images/video across 200 languages, deploys AI agents 5x faster than competitors, and is 60% cheaper than its predecessor. ByteDance launched Doubao 2.0 (reasoning/multi-step tasks matching ChatGPT and Gemini) plus SeeDance 2.0 (AI video generation that went viral but drew copyright criticism from the Motion Picture Association). Zhipu AI released GLM-5, a 744B-parameter open-source model trained entirely on Huawei Ascend chips — zero US semiconductor dependency. All three companies are pushing hard on AI agents that can navigate websites and complete multi-step workflows.
items.relevance: Three things worth noting: (1) Qwen3.5 being 60% cheaper while faster is the cost compression trend continuing — AI gets cheaper fast. (2) GLM-5 running on zero US chips is a geopolitical milestone. (3) The copyright backlash against SeeDance 2.0 is a preview of where all AI video tools are headed legally. For practical use, Qwen3.5's agent speed claims are worth testing if you ever need a cheaper model for batch tasks.

items.title: Former GitHub CEO Launches 'Entire' — $60M to Rebuild Dev Workflows for the Agent Era
items.summary: Thomas Dohmke (former GitHub CEO) launched Entire with a $60M seed round — the largest seed investment ever for developer tools. Backed by Felicis, Madrona, and Microsoft's M12. The thesis: Git tracks what changed but not why. AI agents generate reasoning, prompts, and decision paths that disappear when sessions end. Entire's first open-source product is a Git-aware CLI that automatically captures AI agent context during development — preserving the 'why' alongside the 'what.' Dohmke argues current dev workflows (issues, PRs, reviews) were designed for human-to-human collaboration and can't be retrofitted for human-to-agent work.
items.relevance: This directly addresses a pain point you've probably felt: when Claude Code makes changes, the reasoning behind those changes isn't captured in Git commits. Entire wants to solve that. The open-source CLI could be worth integrating into your workflow — especially for AVA development where you're building complex systems and need to understand 'why did the AI make this choice?' months later. $60M seed says investors think this is a real gap.

items.title: Omnipod 6 Confirmed — Expanding AID to Type 2 Diabetes, New Features Coming
items.summary: HCPLive published details on upcoming Omnipod technology upgrades. Omnipod 6 will target both Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes, significantly expanding automated insulin delivery to the large population of insulin-requiring T2D patients who've had limited pump access. Insulet (Omnipod's maker) reports earnings this week — analyst expectations are for continued strong growth driven by international expansion and the Omnipod 5 installed base. Specific Omnipod 6 feature details and timeline still emerging.
items.relevance: You're on Omnipod 5 — this is literally your next upgrade. Omnipod 6 expanding to T2D is a massive market move: bigger user base means more R&D investment, better insurance coverage momentum, and a larger audience for AVA's educational tools. Insulet earnings this week might reveal more about the Omnipod 6 timeline. Worth watching.

items.title: Claude Code Controversy Continues — File Name Hiding Gets Partial Rollback
items.summary: The Claude Code v2.1.20 change that hid file names from progress output continues to generate backlash. Boris Cherny (Claude Code lead) repurposed verbose mode as a compromise — it now shows file paths for reads/searches without full thinking output. But developers argue this breaks verbose mode for those who actually wanted full details. The core tension: Anthropic is optimizing for longer agentic runs where output volume is overwhelming, while power users need granular visibility for security, catching wrong-context errors, and controlling token spend.
items.relevance: Still evolving — the verbose mode compromise is live now. If you update Claude Code, check your settings: verbose mode has been redefined to mean 'show file paths' rather than 'show everything.' This is a UX philosophy clash that affects daily workflow. The takeaway: Anthropic is building for longer autonomous sessions, which aligns with how you use Claude Code through Clawdbot for extended development sprints.

items.title: Medtronic-Abbott CGM Partnership + MiniMed Go Phone Integration
items.summary: Medtronic announced its MiniMed Go pump now features full real-time CGM integration via smartphone — users can check glucose trends, insulin-on-board, and dosing needs directly from their phones. Separately, Medtronic's partnership with Abbott (announced in 2025) continues expanding: Abbott's CGM sensors are being integrated into Medtronic's insulin delivery and Smart MDI systems, giving users more sensor flexibility within one ecosystem. Medtronic reports strong Q3 FY26 momentum driven by these diabetes technology advances.
items.relevance: The Medtronic-Abbott partnership creating cross-compatible CGM+pump ecosystems is exactly the kind of interoperability the T1D community has wanted for years. Kaislyn's on Tandem+Dexcom and you're on Omnipod+Dexcom, but this trend toward mix-and-match compatibility could eventually mean more freedom to choose the best pump and best CGM independently. Also relevant for AVA: as more devices become phone-integrated, the app ecosystem around diabetes management gets richer.
